The boxes an object's shapes add to bank 4's list at $C000, 42 of eight bytes ($8879): the shape, its first and last column and first and last row, each moved by four times the object's column or row, two bytes moved by where the object stands, and its height, moved by twice the object's.

The records an object's shapes add to bank 3's list of boxes at $C000, 25 of four bytes (first and last across, first and last down), moved by where the object stands ($8879): the ground the actors walk round.

Types $10 to $13's (class 5) sprite frames, 17 of six bytes each ($A493): the width (3 for 16 pixels, 4 for 24), the rows, and the addresses of the picture and its mask. All take the mask built at $8521.
The pictures of types $10 to $13.
Continued from pictures_10 ($DFEE): its bytes from $E000.
For types $18 to $1B, drawn in two pieces ($A725), four bytes for each of 24 frames: the first piece's frame, then the step across and down to the second and its frame.

Continued from masks_18 ($EA3B): its bytes from $F000.
The pictures of types $18 to $1B, continued, then their last masks from $F12B.
The menu pointer's picture, two bytes a row for 13 rows, named by bank 3's $C8B3 and the copy of it at $C8BC; its mask is the 26 bytes that follow, the start of the objects' frame list.

The objects' sprite frames, 20 of six bytes, an object's number being its frame: read for an object on the ground ($F6D6) and for its icon in the bag (bank 3's $C8B3). Objects 9, 10, 17, 18 and 19 take their picture as their mask; objects 0, 3, 5, 6, 7, 11, 12 and 15 the 32 bytes at $F5FB, which begin the frame list of types $1C to $1F. Object 10's picture word, at $F1EF, is changed by bank 3's $FAFF.
The pictures of objects 9 and 0, then the jewel's.

The jewel's three pictures, 16 rows of two bytes from $F25B, $F279 and $F295 (overlapping by two bytes), which bank 3's $FAFF writes into object 10's frame in turn, so that it glints. Its mask stays the first.
The pictures of objects 18, 17 and 1 to 7, the mask at $F3E1, object 8's picture, object 19's, and the masks at $F449 and $F479.
22 bytes among the objects' pictures that no frame names.
The pictures of objects 11 to 16, with the masks at $F544, $F56E and $F5CB among them.

Types $1C to $1F's (class 8) sprite frames, 24 of six bytes each ($A493): the width (3 for 16 pixels, 4 for 24), the rows, and the addresses of the picture and its mask. Its first 32 bytes are also the mask of eight objects.
The pictures of types $1C to $1F.
The masks of types $1C to $1F, $F7F7 and $F830.
Types 4 to $0F's (class 4) sprite frames, 26 of six bytes each ($A493): the width (3 for 16 pixels, 4 for 24), the rows, and the addresses of the picture and its mask.
The pictures of types 4 to $0F.
The masks of types 4 to $0F, $FBE9 and $FC19. Types $20 to $27 take $FBE9 for some frames too, and the rows from $FC19 to $FC5A are also pictures, of types 4 to $0F, $1C to $1F and $20 to $27.
Types $20 to $27's (class 9) sprite frames, 24 of six bytes each ($A493): the width (3 for 16 pixels, 4 for 24), the rows, and the addresses of the picture and its mask.
The pictures of types $20 to $27.
The masks of types $20 to $27, $FE8B and $FEC1.
No frame reaches the last 262 bytes. From $FF00 on they are eight bytes of 0 and eight of $FF in turn, with a few stray bits: the look of memory never written.
